I'm weighing each candidate, starting with "G6PD Nagano." It's the name of a variant of the G6PD enzyme, which makes me question whether it counts as a disease at all, since the title ties it to congenital hemolytic anemia rather than naming the condition itself.

Next I'm checking whether the NCBI Disease corpus would annotate "G6PD Nagano" at all, and I doubt it would. It's a genetic variant of an enzyme, not a disease, so I'd mark it NONE and cite the disease-mention criterion in What to Annotate §1. Moving on to "congenital hemolytic anemia," which looks like a disease class rather than a specific disease.

I'm going through the remaining candidates: "chronic nonspherocytic hemolytic anemia" looks like a class of anemias, and "G6PD deficiency" reads as a specific disease. I'm also weighing "hemolytic crisis" as a discrete acute condition, along with "upper respiratory infection" as a disease category and "infection-induced hemolysis" as a process rather than a disease.
